Two students, A and B, conduct an experiment in an open field. They clap one after another, and the sound is recorded by a smartphone app. The app displays the audio signal as a wave. What can be concluded about the sound waves produced by their claps?

In the slinky experiment, what does the mark on the slinky represent?
A sound wave is created by a piston moving back and forth in a tube. The piston produces compressions and rarefactions alternately. What does this show about the nature of sound waves?

What is transferred when a sound wave propagates through a medium?
A sound wave is produced by a loud sound source and spreads out in all directions. What shape do the waves take as they move away from the source?
A sound wave is produced in a medium and is observed to have particles vibrating parallel to the direction of wave propagation. What type of wave is this, and why?
A student records a sound wave using an app that displays the wave's amplitude. If the amplitude of the wave is doubled, how will the loudness of the sound change?
What is the relationship between the amplitude of a sound wave and the energy it carries?
In an experiment, echoes must arrive at least 0.2 s after the emission of sound. What is the minimum distance required for the reflecting surface, assuming the speed of sound is 343 m/s?
In a large hall, a sound source emits a wave and reflections are heard within 0.05 s. What phenomenon is this?
A sonar signal takes 4 s to return. What is the depth of the ocean at that location if the speed of sound in seawater is 1500 m/s?
If the speed of sound in air is 340 m/s and in steel is 5100 m/s, what is the time difference between the sound reaching Gunjan through air and through steel when the distance is 340 m?

Which of the following is not a factor that contributes to the unique sound of a person's voice?
Based on the passage, which of the following statements about human hearing is correct?
What is the term used to describe how humans perceive the frequency of a sound?

A sound wave is generated in a rectangular room of dimensions 20 m × 20 m × 30 m. The speed of sound is 350 m/s. If the sound wave reflects off the walls, which of the following times could be the time interval between the original sound and the first echo?
If the speed of sound in air is 340 m/s and the frequency of a sound wave is 20 Hz, what is the wavelength of the wave?
Which of the following best describes the motion of particles in a sound wave?

What is the SI unit of the frequency of a sound wave?

What is the relationship between the amplitude of a sound wave and the energy it carries?
What does the time period of a sound wave represent?
What is the minimum distance required for a reflecting surface to produce an echo, assuming the speed of sound is 340 m/s?
A sound wave is produced by a source and propagates through a medium. What is the main reason that the particles of the medium do not travel with the wave?
Which of the following can produce sound?
If a person claps in a corridor and hears an echo after 0.5 s, what is their distance from the wall, assuming the speed of sound is 340 m/s?
A sound wave is produced by a source and travels through a medium. What happens to the particles of the medium as the sound wave passes through it?
In an experiment, a student strikes a tuning fork and brings it close to a water surface. What would the student observe?
